items.caption: How do you get leads through content?
items.transcript: I get 70 million views a month just on Instagram alone. I think 220 million across all my platforms. My content is driven by my audience. Here's what most businesses could do to actually solve this problem. One, record your sales calls. Two, extract the questions you're being asked, create content around that. Three, figure out what is the belief behind what they're actually asking, create content around that. Figure out what you say to them when they say, well, how are you different than everybody else? Create content around that. So essentially what you're doing is you're just taking the sales call, You're atomizing it to the individual pieces of content and then putting that out to the world. And guess what happens to your sales calls? You start getting people to buy quicker, easier because they've already seen the stuff that you're saying on the calls in your content.

items.caption: The most expensive I've learned
items.transcript: This could probably be the most expensive lesson that I feel like I continually have to learn. Why do people love being part of a team? Because they feel supported, they feel like they can grow. I created a framework. It's three Ts. One, the target. When I have a problem that I want to work through with the person, I focus on the problem. I don't focus on the person. The next level is the tone. And the prompt that I use is be curious, Dan. The first step of being curious is asking the other person how they see the problem. And that stops me from coming in hot and coming in critical and coming in full of emotions. And then the third one, and this is the big one, is trust. What I always remind myself to do at the end of a conversation like that is pump up the other person. Leave them feeling bigger. Because if every time there's a problem, I cut them down, cut them down, cut them down, they're going to be scared, hesitant, worried. So for me, it always goes target the problem, tone, curiosity, and trust, leave them bigger.
